name: Havan
desc: Brazilian department store chain selling national and imported goods wholesale and retail through megastores in 23 states.
capacity_detail: Revenue BRL 14.2bn in 2022 (approx USD 2.6bn at about BRL 5.4 per USD)
sponsorships: Brusque Futebol Clube (shirt sponsor); owns esports team Liberty Esports in CBLOL
markets: Brazil: 171 megastores (2022) across 23 states and the Federal District, plus wholesale and retail sales.
rationale: Mass-market retailer already spending on football and esports; F1 Brazil Grand Prix hospitality and broadcast reach suit its national brand campaigns.

name: Cacau Show
desc: Brazilian chocolate and confectionery maker selling through more than 3,700 own-brand stores, also running hotels and parks.
capacity_detail: Revenue BRL 4.02bn in 2022 per company sustainability report cited by Wikipedia (approx USD 745M at about BRL 5.4 per USD)
markets: Brazil: more than 3,700 stores in almost all Brazilian states, plus Brigaderia, Bendito Cacao Resort and amusement parks.
rationale: Large consumer brand that already buys TV-format sponsorships; F1 Brazil and premium gifting could lift its chocolate positioning.

name: Postobón
desc: Colombian beverage company producing soft drinks, waters, juices and beer, with 19 soft-drink plants nationwide.
capacity_detail: Operating revenue COP 2.85 trillion in 2024 per Supersociedades top-1,000 ranking (approx USD 694M at about COP 4,100 per USD)
markets: Colombia: soft drinks, waters, juices, snacks and beer from 19 soft-drink plants and two breweries.
rationale: Mass beverage brand facing PepsiCo-backed and Coca-Cola rivals; F1 content could refresh youth marketing in Colombia.

name: Tiendas D1
desc: Colombian hard-discount grocery chain operating more than 2,750 stores across Colombia under the D1 brand.
ownership: family-owned (Valorem, Santo Domingo family, 59.75%; Capital Group and IHAG Holding 20% each)
capacity_detail: Operating revenue COP 19.44 trillion in 2024 per Supersociedades top-1,000 ranking (approx USD 4.7bn at about COP 4,100 per USD)
markets: Colombia: more than 2,750 discount grocery stores nationwide (2026).
rationale: Very large domestic retailer; limited F1 fit beyond Colombian fan engagement around drivers or broadcast promotions.

name: Colanta
desc: Colombian farmer-owned co-operative manufacturing dairy products, soft drinks, cold cuts and cereals.
capacity_detail: Revenue COP 3.75 trillion in 2023, consolidated reports cited by Wikipedia (approx USD 915M at about COP 4,100 per USD)
markets: Colombia: dairy, beverages, cold cuts and cereals sold nationally from its Antioquia base.
rationale: Large domestic food co-operative; F1 is a weak fit beyond national brand awareness campaigns.

name: Tecnoquímicas
desc: Colombian maker of pharmaceuticals, generics, hygiene, home-care products and diapers, with brands like MK and Winny.
capacity_detail: Revenue COP 3.09 trillion in 2024 (approx USD 754M at about COP 4,100 per USD)
markets: Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Panama, Central America and the Dominican Republic.
rationale: Regional consumer-health brands like MK could use F1 broadcast reach across Andean and Central American markets.

name: Viva Aerobus
desc: Mexican low-cost airline flying an all-Airbus A320-family fleet of 116 aircraft to about 60 destinations.
sponsorships: NBA San Antonio Spurs; NFL Las Vegas Raiders; Liga MX Atlas, Tigres UANL, Club América; baseball Tomateros de Culiacán, Sultanes de Monterrey
markets: Mexico domestic network plus routes to the United States and Central and South America; more than 160 routes.
rationale: Already buys NBA and NFL partnerships; Mexico City Grand Prix and Mexican F1 fandom fit its US-Mexico route marketing.

name: Desjardins Group
desc: Canadian financial services co-operative and largest federation of credit unions in North America, mainly in Quebec and Ontario.
capacity_detail: Revenue CAD 20.32bn in 2021 (approx USD 14.7bn at about CAD 1.38 per USD)
markets: Canada, mainly Quebec and Ontario; development arm active in over 30 developing countries.
rationale: Quebec's dominant financial brand; Canadian Grand Prix in Montreal offers a home-market hospitality and member-engagement platform.

name: Indigo Books & Music
desc: Canadian book, gift and lifestyle retailer, taken private and delisted from the TSX in June 2024.
capacity_detail: Revenue CAD 1.079bn in 2017 (approx USD 780M at about CAD 1.38 per USD)
markets: Canada: book and lifestyle stores plus online retail.
rationale: Domestic bookseller with weak motorsport fit; at most Canadian Grand Prix tie-ins for gift and lifestyle ranges.

name: Mitel
desc: Canadian provider of business phone, unified communications and collaboration systems sold through partners and resellers worldwide.
ownership: private: owned by its lenders since 2025 restructuring
capacity_detail: Revenue CAD 1.27bn in 2025 (approx USD 920M at about CAD 1.38 per USD); exited Chapter 11 in June 2025
markets: Worldwide through offices, partners and resellers serving business communications customers.
rationale: Communications rivals like Cisco Webex sit in F1; post-restructuring Mitel could use a team tie-up to relaunch its brand.

name: Mastellone Hnos
desc: Argentine dairy producer behind La Serenísima, making milk, yoghurts, cheeses and desserts for the domestic market.
ownership: family-owned (Mastellone family, with Dallpoint Investments and Arcor)
capacity_detail: Sales ARS 99,324M in 2021 balances, Mercado 1000 ranking (approx USD 1.0bn at the 2021 average of about ARS 95 per USD)
markets: Argentina: national dairy brand La Serenísima with dairy plants including General Rodríguez and San Luis.
rationale: Argentina's leading dairy brand; renewed Argentine F1 interest could support mass consumer promotions, though fit is limited.

name: Banco Comafi
desc: Argentine privately owned commercial bank serving individuals, small businesses, corporates, trade finance and trust clients.
ownership: private: principal shareholders Guillermo Cervino and Eduardo Maschwitz
capacity_detail: Income ARS 41,952M in 2021 balances, Mercado 1000 ranking (approx USD 440M at the 2021 average of about ARS 95 per USD)
markets: Argentina: retail, SME, corporate, investment and trust banking from its Buenos Aires headquarters.
rationale: Mid-size Argentine bank where Santander and Bradesco use F1; a Colapinto-era tie-in could raise retail brand awareness.

name: Galeno
desc: Argentine healthcare group running the Trinidad, Mitre and San Isidro sanatoriums plus Galeno Seguros and Galeno ART.
capacity_detail: Group sales ARS 121,661M in 2021 balances (Galeno, Galeno Seguros, Galeno ART), Mercado ranking (approx USD 1.28bn at about ARS 95 per USD)
markets: Argentina: private sanatoriums in the Buenos Aires area, property insurance and workers' compensation insurance.
rationale: Large Argentine health brand; limited F1 fit beyond domestic consumer awareness around Argentine driver interest.

name: Amarilo
desc: Colombian developer and manager of residential infrastructure projects, known for its cities-within-cities model, also active in Panama.
capacity_detail: Operating revenue COP 2.19 trillion in 2024 per Supersociedades top-1,000 ranking (approx USD 533M at about COP 4,100 per USD)
markets: Colombia and Panama: residential housing developments and large mixed urban projects.
rationale: Homebuilder selling to aspirational buyers; F1 hospitality could suit premium projects, but overall motorsport fit is weak.
